# Context

This script runs the staggered difference-in-differences regression used to estimate the association between same-insurer coverage and health care use. We used the approach developed by Sun and Abraham: Sun L, Abraham S. Estimating dynamic treatment effects in event studies with heterogeneous treatment effects. *J Econom*. 2021;225(2):175-199.

The unit of analysis is the enrollee x six-month calendar period. Enrollees who transition into same-insurer coverage (as defined in `select_code_to_identify_same_insurer_status.Rmd`) during the study period make up the treatment group, assigned to a "wave" based on the six-month period in which they transition; enrollees who never transition make up the comparison group. This script assumes that assignment has already been made and that the user has an analytic file called `cohort`, with one row per enrollee-period, including:

- bene_id
- study_groupf (treatment wave: 0 for the comparison group, 1-k for the six-month calendar period in which the enrollee transitions to same-insurer coverage)
- periodf (the calendar six-month period, as a factor)
- timef (each period labeled "pre"/"post" the switch, e.g. `pre3`, `post0`; `timef` further collapses the two reference periods, `pre1` and the comparison sentinel, into one `reftime` level -- the omitted reference category in the model formula below)
- group/period indicator columns: a 0/1 column for every treatment group (e.g. `g5`), every calendar period (e.g. `pre3`), and every group-by-period cell that appears in the data (e.g. `g5_pre3`, equal to 1 for enrollees in treatment wave 5 observed at relative period `pre3`) -- the aggregation function below uses these to count how many enrollee-periods fall into each cell being aggregated
- n_mo_period (number of months the enrollee was observed within the period; used as a regression weight)
- state_res, year, state_cnty_fips_cd (state, year, and county identifiers, used for state-by-year fixed effects and county-clustered standard errors)
- ltss_user_type (type of Medicaid LTSS received during the period: home and community-based services, nursing facility, or both)
- 24 time-varying chronic condition indicators from the CMS Chronic Condition Warehouse algorithms
- Kim et al. claims-based frailty_index score
- the outcome variable for the model being run (e.g. `ed`, `hosp`, `op_visits`, `pqi_90_num`, `los`, `readmission`, `discharge_home` -- as built in the `select_code_to_identify_*.Rmd` scripts, aggregated to the enrollee-period level)


## Model specification

The model is specified as:

Y_it = a_i + l_t + d_(s(i),y(t)) + sum_g sum_(l != -1) b_(g,l) * 1[G_i = g] * 1[t - G_i = l] + X_it'g + e_it

where Y_it is the outcome for enrollee i in six-month period t; a_i are enrollee fixed effects; l_t are calendar-period fixed effects; d_(s(i),y(t)) are state-by-year fixed effects; G_i is enrollee i's treatment wave (0 for comparison enrollees); and X_it is a vector of the time-varying covariates listed above. The interaction terms 1[G_i=g] x 1[t-G_i=l] estimate the treatment effect b_(g,l) at each relative period l for each treatment wave g, relative to the period immediately preceding the switch (l = -1), which serves as the reference period. Standard errors are clustered at the county level, and observations are weighted by the number of months the enrollee was observed in the period (`n_mo_period`).

Below, set `outcome` to the name of the outcome variable you want to model (e.g. `outcome <- "ed"`).


# Subset for secondary outcomes

Length of stay, readmission, and discharge home are only defined for enrollee-periods at risk for that outcome (i.e. those with a qualifying hospitalization), using the denominator flags built in `select_code_to_identify_all-cause_hospitalizations.Rmd`.

```{r}
if (outcome == "los")            cohort <- cohort[los_den >= 1]
if (outcome == "readmission")    cohort <- cohort[readmission_den >= 1]
if (outcome == "discharge_home") cohort <- cohort[discharge_home_den >= 1]
```


# Model call

```{r}
f <- as.formula(paste0(
  outcome,
  " ~ study_groupf + i(timef, study_groupf, ref = 'reftime') + ltss_user_type + ",
  "adrd + ami + anemia + asthma + atrial_fib + bph + any_cancer + cataract + chronickidney + copd + ",
  "depression + diabetes + glaucoma + hf + hip + hlp + hypertension + hypothyroid + ischemic + ",
  "osteoporosis + parkinson + pneumonia + arthritis + stroke + frailty_index | bene_id + periodf + state_res^year"
))

model <- fixest::feols(f, data = cohort, weights = ~n_mo_period, cluster = ~state_cnty_fips_cd)

summary(model)
```

## Get variance-covariance matrix

```{r}
vcov_matrix <- as.matrix(vcov(model))
```


# Aggregate Sun and Abraham estimates

Each group-by-period coefficient (e.g. `g5_pre3`) is a treatment effect estimate for one treatment wave at one relative time period. To get an overall effect across waves for a period of interest (or across waves and periods, e.g. all post-treatment periods combined), we average the relevant coefficients, weighting by each wave's share of enrollee-periods, and obtain the standard error of that weighted average via the delta method.

This function can be used to build any aggregate estimate of interest by passing it the names of the coefficients (`vars_to_avg`) to average together. See Sun and Abraham (2021) for additional detail on constructing these aggregates.

```{r}
agg_coefficients <- function(model, vars_to_avg, data, vcov_matrix) {

  # each wave's share of enrollee-periods among the coefficients being averaged
  Ns <- sapply(vars_to_avg, function(x) nrow(data[get(x) == 1, ]))
  pct_of_pop <- Ns / sum(Ns)

  # weighted average of the coefficient estimates
  estimates <- sapply(vars_to_avg, function(x) model$coefficients[names(model$coefficients) == x])
  estimate <- sum(pct_of_pop * estimates)

  # standard error of the weighted average, via the delta method
  var_matrix <- vcov_matrix[vars_to_avg, vars_to_avg]
  weights <- as.matrix(pct_of_pop)
  se <- as.vector(sqrt(t(weights) %*% var_matrix %*% weights))

  # two-sided t-test
  df <- df.residual(model)
  p <- 2 * pt(abs(estimate / se), df, lower = FALSE)

  data.table(Estimate = round(estimate, 4), SE = round(se, 4),
            LB = round(estimate - 1.96 * se, 4), UB = round(estimate + 1.96 * se, 4), P = round(p, 4))
}
```
